target.title: ProxyFix: use the original client address
target.description: Behind several proxies, X-Forwarded-For lists every hop. Use the first entry, which is the original client, instead of counting from the right. Also simplifies the host:port split for X-Forwarded-Host.

summary: ProxyFix now takes the first entry from X-Forwarded-For instead of indexing from the right based on the trusted count, and simplifies IPv6 host/port splitting for X-Forwarded-Host.

suspects.title: IPv6 host parsing without brackets might incorrectly split port
suspects.problem: Removing the check for `x_host.endswith("]")` means an IPv6 address without a port (like `2001:db8::1`) containing colons will now be incorrectly split by `rsplit(":", 1)`, treating the last segment of the IPv6 address as the `SERVER_PORT` and the remainder as `SERVER_NAME`.
suspects.how_to_check: Search the repository for tests covering X-Forwarded-Host with IPv6 addresses and check how `rsplit` behaves when given an IPv6 address string without brackets.

suspects.title: Ignoring trusted hops count for X-Forwarded-For
suspects.problem: By always taking `values[0]` instead of using `trusted` to select the appropriate proxy hop, an untrusted client can spoof the `X-Forwarded-For` header if there are untrusted proxies or if the application sits behind a trusted reverse proxy that doesn't strip or overwrite client-supplied headers.
suspects.how_to_check: Check the documentation and tests for ProxyFix configuration to see how `x_for` or `trusted` parameter is defined and expected to restrict which proxy hops are trusted.

arguments.claim: Removing the check x_host.endswith("]") causes an IPv6 address without brackets and containing colons (such as 2001:db8::1) to be incorrectly split by rsplit(":", 1) when passed via X-Forwarded-Host.
arguments.suggested_fix: Restore the check `if ":" in x_host and not x_host.endswith("]"):` or handle IPv6 parsing robustly.
arguments.explanation: Without checking whether an IPv6 address is enclosed in brackets (i.e. ending with ']'), an unbracketed IPv6 address such as '2001:db8::1' contains colons, so `x_host.rsplit(':', 1)` splits the last segment (e.g. '1') off as `SERVER_PORT` and treats the rest ('2001:db8:') as `SERVER_NAME`, corrupting the host configuration.

evidence.note: ProxyFix parses x_host by splitting on the rightmost colon if ":" in x_host, without checking if it is an IPv6 address enclosed in square brackets.
Test case passes [2001:db8::a] with brackets for ipv6 host.

This matches the claim that the change uses the leftmost (potentially client-spoofed) IP instead of selecting the correct proxy hop based on the trusted proxy count.
